payload.claim: The `revert_gate` docstring says the fifth skip case 'touches both `reverted` and `run_tests`, only where a rewritten test is found through `locations`', then describes that very case with the clause 'a diff adding neither a new test nor one rewritten in place.' That description states the opposite of the triggering condition: the code only enters the reverted-tree block and calls `run_tests` on `rewritten_pool` (lines 307-316, 385-394, 417-455) when `rewritten_pool` is non-empty, i.e. when a rewritten test IS found, not when neither is found. As written the sentence also omits that this same fifth case covers 'every new test is exempt' (the other branch of `skip_summary`, line 305), not only 'a diff adding no new test.' A reader using this docstring to reason about when the gate touches the reverted tree would conclude the opposite of what the code does.
